deep_analysis.executive_intro:
The FTSE screen is broadly neutral-to-cautious: 146 names sit on Hold versus 59 actionable Buys (19 Strong Buy, 40 Buy) and 43 Avoids, so value signals are concentrated rather than market-wide. Among the five top Strong Buy candidates, Industrials dominate (FGP.L, MEGP.L, JSG.L), with single representatives from Healthcare (HIK.L) and Communication Services (ITV.L). Quantitative support is uneven — model pass rates range from 8/22 (JSG.L) to 15/22 (FGP.L, MEGP.L, ITV.L) — and every top name carries a “new” signal with conviction in the low-to-mid 40s–50s range, limiting timing confidence. A key data caution: several names show material free-cash-flow basis mismatches (filing vs screen TTM vs company-adjusted figures), and FGP.L in particular shows a Yahoo D/E of 161% against filing-adjusted net debt of £137.7m, meaning headline leverage and cash-flow metrics should be verified before sizing positions.

FGP.L (FirstGroup plc, Industrials) passes 15 of 22 models with an 86% composite score (87% sector-relative), clearing Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Lynch PEG (PEG 0.55, growth 16%), and Piotroski F-Score (8/9) on metrics of P/E 8.7, P/B 1.3, yield 4.0%, and ROE 16.7%. It fails Graham Defensive and Financial Health on weak liquidity (current ratio 0.73), and Economic Moat on sub-threshold ROE/ROA/margins. With three of five top picks in Industrials, sector concentration is meaningful. Verdict: watchlist — attractive cheapness and quality scores are offset by FCF divergence (filing £362.6M vs screen TTM £302.8M vs company-adj £73.8M), the leverage override, and an adjusted signal of Buy rather than Strong Buy.

HIK.L (Hikma Pharmaceuticals, Healthcare) passes 11/22 models (81% composite, 91% sector-relative) including Graham Enterprising, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, and Financial Health, on P/E 12.4, P/B 1.9, yield 3.9%, and ROE 15.4%. It fails FCF Yield (3.6%, below 5% threshold), Lynch PEG (growth 1.7%, PEG 7.08), Piotroski F-Score (6/9), and Earnings Quality (weak free-cash conversion); net FCF dividend coverage is 0.64×. Healthcare is a lone sector representative among top picks, so concentration risk is low. Verdict: watchlist — sector-relative ranking is strong, but stagnant earnings growth and cash-conversion weakness undermine the dividend/GARP case.

MEGP.L (ME Group International, Industrials) passes 15/22 models (82% composite, 88% sector-relative), notably Economic Moat, High Dividend Yield, Buffett Quality, and Magic Formula, on P/E 8.1, P/B 2.3, yield 6.5%, and ROE 28.2%. It fails Lynch PEG (growth 0.4%), Piotroski F-Score (6/9), and Earnings Quality; an interim-quality overlay flags declining interim EPS and net FCF/dividend coverage of 0.84× (gross 1.68×). Industrials concentration applies here as well. Verdict: accumulate — the widest moat and yield profile in the group, but size modestly given near-term earnings softness and sub-1× net dividend coverage.

ITV.L (ITV plc, Communication Services) passes 15/22 models (82% composite, 86% sector-relative) including High Dividend Yield (7.1%, universe rank 98%), Lynch PEG (PEG 0.51, growth 23%), FCF Yield (7.3%), and Earnings Quality, on P/E 11.6 and P/B 1.5. It fails Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, and Piotroski F-Score (3/9 — the weakest financial-trend score among top picks). RSI 34 and price below the 200-day MA suggest a downtrend despite neutral timing. Verdict: watchlist — the yield and growth metrics are compelling, but deteriorating financial momentum (F-Score 3/9) warrants confirmation that earnings quality is sustainable.

JSG.L (Johnson Service Group, Industrials) passes only 8/22 models despite an 85% composite score, with a below-peer 74% sector-relative rank. Key passes are FCF Yield (19.1%), Piotroski F-Score (7/9), and Earnings Quality; failures span Earnings Yield, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple (EV/EBIT 13.6), Dreman Contrarian, and Financial Health (weak liquidity, current ratio 0.93). FCF basis mismatch is flagged (filing $100.6M vs screen TTM $27.4M). Industrials concentration is the third name in this sector cluster. Verdict: pass — the thinnest multi-model support in the top five, combined with liquidity concerns and FCF inconsistency, does not justify priority allocation.

- FGP.L: Public-transport contract and regulatory renewal risk (concession terms, fare caps) is not captured by the screen; open question whether defined-benefit pension obligations exist and how lease liabilities (Yahoo D/E 161% vs filing-adjusted £137.7m net debt) affect true economic leverage.
- HIK.L: Generic-pharma regulatory risk (FDA approvals, plant inspections) and patent-cliff timing are absent from quantitative inputs; open question on pipeline depth given earnings growth of just 1.7% and net FCF dividend coverage of 0.64×.
- MEGP.L: Business-model cyclicality and technology-disruption risk (automated photo booths, payment terminals) are not screened; open question on geographic/customer concentration and whether the 6.5% yield is sustainable with net FCF/dividend coverage at 0.84× and statutory earnings growth of 0.4%.
- ITV.L: Structural decline in linear-TV advertising and streaming competition are qualitative risks outside the model set; open question on content-investment requirements and governance around the dividend (7.1% yield) given Piotroski F-Score 3/9 and prior-year OCF/FCF declines (OCF £202M vs £333M prior; FCF £187M vs £284M prior).
- JSG.L: Hospitality and healthcare-laundry cyclicality (occupancy-driven volumes) is not explicitly flagged; open question on contract pricing power and balance-sheet resilience given current ratio 0.93 and failure on Financial Health (weak liquidity).

documents.name: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC
documents.executive_summary: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC (HIK.L) is a FTSE 100 generics and specialty pharmaceutical group with a three-segment model: US-focused Injectables and Hikma Rx, plus fast-growing Branded MENA. The quantitative screen rates the name a strong buy (11/22 models; composite 81%), driven by cheapness (P/E 12.4, P/B 1.9), a 3.9% yield, solid ROE (15.4%), and investment-grade leverage (net debt/core EBITDA 1.6x at FY2025). Filings show earnings recovery after a difficult 2023: FY2025 core operating profit reached $741m on revenue of $3,349m, and H1 2026 delivered a 9% core operating profit beat with guidance reiterated. The valuation hook is a quality generic franchise trading below peers after a February 2026 guidance reset and management shuffle, partially offset by a $250m buyback. The key debate is whether Branded and Hikma Rx momentum can outweigh Injectables margin compression, heavy capex, and weak reported free cash flow ($119m in FY2025 vs $185m dividends) — a divergence the screen itself flags.
documents.investment_thesis: For a value investor, Hikma offers a rare combination: a profitable, diversified generic platform at a mid-cycle multiple, with tangible capital return (5% dividend growth; $250m buyback largely executed by August 2026) and improving broker sentiment after H1 results. The screen passes five factor families — cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk — including Graham Enterprising, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, and Financial Health. Business quality is supported by filing disclosures: largest pharma company by sales in MENA, third-largest US injectables supplier by volume, BBB/stable ratings from S&P and Fitch, and ROIC of 16.0% in FY2025. Statutory EPS growth (182 cents in 2025 vs 162 cents in 2024) and core EPS stability (228 cents vs 224 cents) underpin the earnings-yield case. The screen fails FCF Yield, Lynch PEG, and Economic Moat models for identifiable reasons — low headline growth (~1.7%), thin FCF conversion, and sub-moat ROE/margins — which a value investor can accept if Injectables stabilises and capex normalises. H1 2026 progress (Branded revenue +15%, core group operating profit +9%) suggests the FY2026 core operating profit range of $720m–$770m is achievable, supporting the screen’s strong-buy signal while warranting scrutiny of cash conversion rather than outright rejection.
documents.financial_review:
Primary sources: FY2025 results (`ir_0e40d9707e30c3b7.txt`), FY2025 annual report (`ir_3a67962eb8770824.txt`), refetched Companies House FY2025 extract (`ch_05557934_MzUxODk1NDgyN2FkaXF6a2N4.txt`), H1 2026 interim (`5f26e81d036b3596.txt`), April 2026 trading update (`94eb1f8d38a51fa6.txt`). Yahoo `financials_annual.json` used only for pre-2024 trend context.

**FY2025 (year ended 31 December 2025)** — corroborated across IR press release and refetched CH body

| Metric | 2025 | 2024 | Change |
|--------|------|------|--------|
| Revenue | $3,349m | $3,127m | +7% |
| Core revenue | $3,349m | $3,156m | +6% |
| Core operating profit | $741m | $719m | +3% |
| Reported operating profit | $542m | $612m | −11% |
| Profit to shareholders | $402m | $359m | +12% |
| Core profit to shareholders | $503m | $495m | +2% |
| Core basic EPS | 228c | 224c | +2% |
| Reported basic EPS | 182c | 162c | +12% |
| Dividend per share | 84c | 80c | +5% |
| Operating cash flow | $436m | $564m | −23% |
| Net debt | $1,387m | — | 1.6× net debt/core EBITDA |

Reported operating profit was reduced by the sodium oxybate legal settlement; excluding ~$186m settlement-related cash, management states operating cash flow would have risen ~10%. Segment mix unchanged from prior memo: Injectables core revenue +7% but core operating profit −6% (margin 31.0%); Branded core revenue +10% with core operating profit +19%; Hikma Rx flat revenue, core operating profit +5%.

**Pipeline and launch cadence (refetch adds corroboration, not new totals)**

Annual report (`ir_3a67962eb8770824.txt`): 300+ products in pipeline, 84 launches, five-year revenue CAGR +7%. Refetched CH body (`ch_05557934_MzUxODk1NDgyN2FkaXF6a2N4.txt`) independently confirms 84 launches and 99 approvals in 2025. FY2025 press release: 118 Injectables pipeline products (15 ready-to-use). Prior-year CH extract (`ch_05557934_MzQ2NDU3ODU0NmFkaXF6a2N4.txt`) shows 132 launches in 2024 for historical context. This active pipeline partially offsets the screen's 1.7% statutory EPS growth input but does not provide dated patent-cliff revenue exposure.

**Free cash flow and dividend coverage (unchanged; CH bodies silent)**

From `ir_0e40d9707e30c3b7.txt` cash flow statement: OCF $436m less PPE capex $197m and intangible purchases $120m ≈ **$119m FCF**. Dividends paid $185m; net FCF/dividend coverage **0.64×** per `screening_snapshot.json` (gross ~1.31×). FY2026 capex guide $190m–$210m plus $120m partner-reimbursed CMO spend. Refetched CH accounts do not include a cash-flow statement; FCF figures are not inferable from CH bodies alone.

**H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026)**

| Metric | H1 2026 | H1 2025 | Change |
|--------|---------|---------|--------|
| Revenue | $1,728m | $1,658m | +4% |
| Core operating profit | $405m | $373m | +9% |
| Core basic EPS | 128c | 122c | +5% |
| Operating cash flow | $214m | $161m | +33% |
| Interim dividend | 38c/sh | 36c/sh | +6% |
| Net debt / core EBITDA | 1.9x | — | up from 1.6x |

Pipeline H1 2026: 48 submissions, 40 approvals, 43 launches; R&D $86m (5.0% of revenue, +18%). Branded revenue +15%; Injectables flat (core margin 27.6%); Hikma Rx flat with margin 20.6%.

**Remaining gaps**

Patent-cliff timing by product/year absent from all 73 indexed bodies including the three refetched CH extracts. Yahoo quarterly cashflow empty — TTM FCF ($14.4m in screen) unverified. Medium-term group and Injectables margin guidance withdrawn February 2026. No structured FCF bridge in `ir_presentation_metrics.json` beyond a single OCF highlight.

documents.risks_and_flags:
**Evident from filings (including refetched CH bodies)**

| Risk | Evidence | Status |
|------|----------|--------|
| Regulatory / cGMP | H1 2026 principal risks: Product quality and safety (cGMP/cGLP/cGDP); 13 US FDA-inspected plants and 29 total manufacturing sites (`ir_3a67962eb8770824.txt`); CH bodies state plants are "regularly inspected by the US FDA" (`ch_05557934_MzQ2NDU3ODU0NmFkaXF6a2N4.txt`) | Evidenced; no Form 483 or warning letter in indexed bodies |
| Litigation | Sodium oxybate settlement (~$186m cash FY2025); Amarin skinny-label dismissed (H1 2026); contingent IP matters in FY2025 notes (`ir_0e40d9707e30c3b7.txt`) | Evidenced |
| Injectables margin / competition | Margin 35.3% → 31.0% → 27.6% (H1 2026); FY2026 guide 27%–28%; US competition on high-value products cited | Evidenced |
| Geopolitical (MENA) | H1 principal-risk update: Middle East conflict increased crisis/disruption exposure | Evidenced |
| US tariffs | H1 discusses potential generic import tariffs; cites US manufacturing footprint | Evidenced; outcome open |
| Leverage / FCF | Net debt/EBITDA 1.4x → 1.6x → 1.9x; FCF ~$119m vs dividends $185m; buyback $175m H1 2026 | Evidenced |
| Customer concentration | Two US wholesalers ~11% of group revenue each (H1 2026) | Evidenced |
| Governance / key person | CEO/CFO/board changes Feb 2026; acting CFO; medium-term guidance withdrawn | Evidenced |
| Pipeline execution | 300+ pipeline, 99 approvals, 84 launches (2025) documented across IR and refetched CH body; revenue timing uncertain | Partially evidenced |

**Still open (alternate source needed)**

- **Patent-cliff timing:** No product-level expiry schedule in refetched CH bodies or IR extracts. Would unlock: Orange Book / IQVIA product revenue schedules.
- **FDA inspection outcomes:** Filings assert compliance and FDA-inspected status but do not record recent inspection classifications. Would unlock: FDA inspection database by facility.

documents.name: ME Group International plc
documents.executive_summary: ME Group International plc operates a global estate of ~49,000 self-service vending units, chiefly photobooths (Photo.ME) and unattended laundry (Wash.ME), across 16 countries. The quantitative screen rates the name a strong buy on cheapness (P/E ~8.1, yield ~6.5%), quality (ROE ~28%), dividend, GARP and risk metrics, with filing-aligned FY25 free cash flow of $25.2m supporting the valuation hook. FY25 delivered record profit before tax of £78.2m and a strategic pivot toward higher-margin laundry, but H1 FY26 shows softer momentum: profit before tax fell 3.8% to £32.7m, FY26 guidance was cut to £69–74m, and the interim dividend was reduced. The central debate is whether laundry rollout, the ASDA partnership and capital returns offset photobooth regulatory drag in Germany, cyclical weakness in France, FX headwinds and governance noise from audit delays and cash-classification restatements.
documents.investment_thesis: The screen’s strong-buy signal rests on a credible value stack: 15 of 22 models pass, composite score 82%, debt/equity ~28%, and a business generating strong operating cash flow (£115.5m in FY25 per the 2025 Annual Results RNS) against a market capitalisation that implies mid-single-digit earnings and high-single-digit FCF yields. Business quality supports the cheapness case: ME Group holds leading photobooth positions, long-dated site contracts (no single customer above 2% of turnover), and a fast-growing laundry division that contributed 46% of group EBITDA in FY25 and exceeded photobooth EBITDA contribution in H1 FY26 (53.9% of group EBITDA). Capital allocation is shareholder-friendly: FY25 total dividend of 8.64p (+9.5%), an £18m buyback launched in March 2026, and net cash of £26.5m at 31 October 2025 (£7.5m at 30 April 2026 after capex, dividends and buybacks). For a value investor, the thesis is a cash-generative, asset-heavy franchise trading at a discount because near-term earnings are decelerating, the market prices in Germany ID-photo regulation and April 2026 consumer softness, and headline growth is negligible (statutory EPS growth ~0.4% on the screen). The screen’s interim-quality overlay (interim EPS decline, net FCF/dividend coverage below 1.0×) already moderated the signal to Buy; deep research largely confirms the valuation case but does not fully dismiss the quality concerns behind that overlay.

**Technology / regulatory disruption (evidenced, not payment terminals):** Filings frame disruption as ID-photo centralisation and technology obsolescence in photobooth systems (`f40be706e75a10ae.txt` — “Centralisation of the production of ID photos”; “Failure to keep up with advances in technology”). German passport-photo rules continue to weigh on Photo.ME; next-generation compliant booths from H2 FY26. No filing reference to payment-terminal exposure. **Open:** smartphone/home-capture adoption beyond disclosed regulatory channels.

**Geographic concentration (evidenced):** CE 68.3% of FY25 revenue; France >50% of photobooth revenue only (`ir_9ac08315f9388f7e.txt`). Principal risks note dependence on trading conditions in France and the UK. **Open:** exact France share of group revenue.

documents.name: ITV plc
documents.executive_summary: ITV plc screens as a **strong buy** on quantitative value metrics (15/22 models passing; composite score 82%; P/E 11.6, P/B 1.5, dividend yield 7.1%), underpinned by resilient cash generation, a fixed 5.0p ordinary dividend (~£190m annually), and a pending **£950m** shareholder return from the agreed sale of Media & Entertainment (M&E) to Sky for up to **£1.6bn**. The investment case rests on whether today’s valuation adequately prices a business transitioning from integrated broadcaster-producer to a **Studios-centric pure play**, with ITVX and linear broadcast economics largely exiting at completion (expected H2 2027, subject to CMA/regulatory clearance). The central debate is valuation methodology: screens reflect consolidated pre-deal earnings and yield, while post-deal ITV will be smaller, less diversified, and more exposed to global content cycles—offset by capital return, a **£2.1bn** minimum content-supply commitment from Sky/M&E (2028–2032), and management’s target of investment-grade leverage at ~1.5x net debt/EBITDA.
documents.investment_thesis:
The quantitative screen aligns with a credible value setup. ITV passes five model families—**cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk**—with a sector-relative composite of 86% and full data quality (20/20 metrics). Headline multiples are attractive for a business generating adjusted EBITA margins above 15% at group level historically, with debt/equity of 52% and net leverage of 1.0x at FY 2025 (filing). Dividend-oriented screens (High Dividend Yield, Dividend Growth, Low P/E + High Yield) and cash-yield models (FCF Yield, Earnings Yield, Acquirer’s Multiple) all pass, consistent with a contrarian UK media name trading below long-run earnings power.

Business quality supports the screen, with caveats. **ITV Studios** is a scaled global producer (10% external revenue growth in FY 2025; adjusted EBITA £297m at 13.9% margin) benefiting from streaming-platform demand and high-margin catalogue/digital distribution (Zoo 55). **M&E** remains the UK’s largest commercial broadcaster and ad-funded streamer: digital revenue reached **£614m** (+10%) in FY 2025, ITVX streaming hours +16%, and cumulative ITVX investment was recouped four years ahead of plan. Management has delivered **£253m** of permanent non-content savings since 2019. Two-thirds of revenue now comes from Studios and digital M&E—the strategic pivot the screen partially captures via earnings resilience and dividend continuity.

What the screen underweights is **event risk and pro-forma economics**. The Sky transaction unlocks ~25p/share of cash return and simplifies the equity story, but completion is 12–18 months away, may require Phase 2 CMA review, and leaves a less diversified earnings base. Failed screens (Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, Piotroski F-Score 3/9) flag middling ROE (13.5%), thin broadcast margins, and deteriorating year-on-year financial momentum indicators—consistent with a cyclical advertising business, not a wide-moat compounder. For a value investor, the strong-buy signal is best read as **“cheap consolidated cash flow plus catalyst,”** not “quality compounder at any price.”

post_run_review.executive_summary: This run produced 59 buy-tier names (19 Strong Buy, 40 Buy) against 146 Hold and 43 Avoid, but conviction on top picks is capped: every named Strong Buy carries a “new” signal with conviction in the low-to-mid 40s–50s, and model pass rates span 8/22 (JSG.L) to 15/22 (FGP.L, MEGP.L, ITV.L). The dominant systemic weakness is not filing volume—buy-tier coverage is deep (20 tickers, zero in `thin_filing_tickers`, only FGP.L and IMB.L with one indexed-without-body each)—but inconsistent cash-flow and leverage metadata: filing vs screen TTM vs company-adjusted FCF diverge materially on HIK.L, FGP.L, ITV.L, and JSG.L, and Yahoo D/E on FGP.L (161%) conflicts with filing-adjusted net debt (£137.7m). Gap-fill updated three memos (HIK.L, MEGP.L, ITV.L) to version 3 with “strong” grades, yet all nine follow-up questions remain only partially resolved and deep-analysis verdicts stay watchlist on FGP.L, HIK.L, and ITV.L versus accumulate on MEGP.L. These scoring-metadata and ingest-quality gaps do not invalidate cheapness signals but they block full conviction and position sizing on top picks until FCF bridges, quarterly cash-flow series, and cross-ticker divergence flags are automated.

rules: Universe: only strong_buy / buy names from the latest screen.
Timing filter: names with timing_signal=wait are excluded from new buys.
Sector cap: at most 1 name(s) per known sector (cap=20%).
Ranking: highest conviction_score first, keep at most 3 names.
Sizing: equal-weight sleeves of current NAV after exits; buys limited by remaining cash.
Hold buffer: full exit only after 2 consecutive rebalance(s) outside the target set.
Re-entry cooldown: wait 1 rebalance(s) after a full exit before buying the same name again.
Dust guard: skip trim/top-up adjustments below £10.
plan.summary: Next rebalance would target 3 equal-weight sleeve(s).

question_outcomes.question: Is the 7.1% dividend sustainable through the advertising cycle, given Piotroski F-Score 3/9 and declining operating cash flow?
question_outcomes.evidence: FY 2025 filing body (`29bdb56d3cedb539.txt`) shows statutory net cash from operating activities **£202m** (2024: £333m), company-adjusted FCF **£187m**, and ordinary dividend **5.0p (~£190m)**—essentially 1.0x coverage on adjusted FCF, sub-1.0x on Yahoo statutory FCF **£148m** (OCF £202m − capex £54m, `financials_annual.json`). Profit-to-cash fell to **65%** (from 83%); H1 2026 rolling conversion **63%** with H1 FCF **£40m** (`b2cc897fdad7e822.txt`). Management nonetheless maintained 5.0p FY 2025 and H1 2026 interim 1.7p unchanged, stating intent for “at least 5.0p” full-year with medium-term growth (`b2cc897fdad7e822.txt`). Liquidity remains robust (£1,327m FY 2025; £1,304m H1 2026) and going concern is affirmed (`29bdb56d3cedb539.txt`). Piotroski 3/9 reflects deteriorating **momentum**, not negative earnings or negative OCF. Near-term sustainability relies on balance-sheet liquidity and management discretion rather than comfortable FCF headroom; ~£950m Sky capital return (`10f52d865099383d.txt`) would transform capacity but is not available until expected H2 2027 completion.
